subject: Re: ACME evaluation — resource guarantees, burst policy & kickoff
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + draft POC plan (capacity & success criteria)

Hi Emily — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned before drafting the trial agreement:

What we heard from you:
- Goal: validate model latency and throughput for real-time customer-facing chat (multi-turn, up to ~4k tokens).
- Success criteria you care about: 95th latency SLA, steady-state throughput target, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Security: VPC isolation and audit logs required for procurement.

Proposal (high level):
- Reserved baseline: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state serving (handles ~12–18 requests/sec depending on prompt length).
- Autoscaling policy: burst up to 8 GPUs for short windows (10–15 mins) with cooldowns; target autoscale threshold at queue depth or 95th-pct latency breach.
- Caching: we’ll enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts to reduce token compute.
- Timeline: kickoff within 2 weeks after the SOW + trial agreement; 3-week evaluation window (1 week canary, 2 weeks load/quality testing).

Attached: draft POC plan (acme_poc_plan_v1.pdf) and ballpark cost estimates (acme_poc_capacity_costs.xlsx).

Ask: can you confirm the success criteria below (or propose edits) so we can lock resources and finalize the DocuSign?
- Functional: 95th-pct latency < 200ms for up to 4k tokens (95th-pct measured at Redwood Console).
- Throughput: sustained 12–15 req/s with occasional bursts to 60 req/s for up to 10 mins.
- Quality: fewer than 2% prompt failures / hallucinations on the evaluation prompt set (we’ll work with your dataset).

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Marissa to own onboarding and Dev to finalize the autoscale/VM sizing details.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Thanks, Karthik — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side before we sign:

Success criteria edits:
- Latency: we’re comfortable with 95th < 250ms for 4k tokens (measured end-to-end). If Redwood can demonstrate consistent <200ms on your staging run, that’s a win.
- Throughput: target 15 req/s steady; bursts up to 4x sustained for 10 minutes is acceptable. We’ll provide a representative traffic trace.
- Cost: we need a ballpark of cost per 1k tokens for forecasting — the spreadsheet helps but can you include a conservative scenario with burst pricing?

Security/procurement asks:
- VPC peering and customer-managed keys (KMS) are must-haves.
- SOC2 evidence + audit logs for the trial duration.
- Legal will want a short trial SOW + liability/PD clauses; helpful if you can pre-populate the SOW for review.

Finally, looping in Nathan (ML infra) to coordinate load tests. We’d like Redwood to provision a sandbox environment where we can point our load generator and run an initial canary.

Can we aim to start the trial week of Nov 8? That gives legal time to look.

—Emily
Director of Product, Acme Tech

Hi Emily — quick technical response to match the asks and make the canary safe to run:

1) Capacity & an example mapping:
- Baseline reservation: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (this maps to ~12–18 req/s at median prompt lengths).
- Burst headroom: we can allow autoscale up to 8 GPUs (4x baseline) via pre-warmed instances; expected spin-up time for a warm node is ~45–60s.
- For immediate short bursts (first 10–60s) we rely on KV/prefix cache + concurrent replicas to keep latency low.

2) Autoscale policy proposal:
- Scale up triggers: queue depth > 20 or 95th-pct latency > 180ms sustained for 30s.
- Maximum burst window: 10 minutes per incident, followed by a 5-minute cooldown.
- Forced fallback: if memory pressure or OOM risk, we’ll gracefully reject excess requests with clear error codes and fallback to a smaller model variant.

3) Instrumentation & logs:
- We’ll enable token-level latency tracing and per-request debug ids; Redwood Console will expose 95/99 latency graphs and cost breakdown by route.
- Audit logs (API, auth events) can be forwarded to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export.

4) Sandbox & canary plan:
- We can provision a sandbox VPC with 1 GPU for the canary (1–2 days) to validate hooking your load generator. If that looks good, we’ll scale to baseline reservation.

Attached: updated capacity workbook with burst scenario (acme_poc_capacity_costs.xlsx).

If you’re comfortable, we’ll hold the baseline reservation provisionally during legal review for 7 days. Let me know preferred timezone/time for a short kickoff.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
